description: The one thing terminal-control writes: an allocation record published once at allocate (or attach), plus one-shot markers. Everything else (is the pane alive, what runs in it, which panes a tab holds) is read live from the driver.

location.incarnationId: <bootId>-<pid>-<startTime> of the multiplexer server; a different server incarnation is a different directory, so records of a dead server never match a live pane
location.publish: write to a temp file in the same directory, fsync, link(2) to the final name; EEXIST means the record already exists and is never overwritten

serverIncarnation.endpoint: socket path the incarnation was read from

launch-requested.rule: written after the ready-shell handshake, immediately before the launch line is typed

released.until: retain only: epoch ms or null

rules: no holder of a slot is stored: who may use a slot is the upper layer's business
a record is never edited; state changes are new markers
records of another incarnation are invalid for every operation and only reported by reconcile-scan
